title: Discount Authorization Matrix and Pricebook Live-Sync Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create an operational playbook and approval automation for enterprise discounts that (1) defines a clear authorization matrix for delegated approvals, (2) introduces a live-sync mechanism to keep the canonical pricebook in sync with finance/billing, and (3) provides guardrails and audit trails tied to security questionnaire (SQ) and contract terms.

Background: We frequently see ad-hoc discount approvals for large enterprise deals that create downstream reconciliation work in finance and billing. Existing pricebook updates are manual, leading to out-of-sync invoice behavior and delays in contract finalization. This ticket consolidates the governance model and builds the minimal automation required to reduce manual steps for common discount bands while preserving escalation for exceptions and SQ-linked concessions.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A documented Discount Authorization Matrix exists and covers at least the following bands: 0-10% (AE delegated), 10-25% (Head of Sales approval), 25-40% (Revenue leadership + Finance review), >40% (VP Exec review + Legal signoff).

A2: Pricebook Live-Sync implementation (webhook + reconciliation job) is able to push approved special price entries to the canonical pricebook in Finance (staging) and reconcile differences nightly; test run demonstrates zero manual edits for 3 sample deals.
A3: SQ gating: any discount >25% or any request tied to data residency/compliance flags must trigger the SQ checklist requirement and block automated approval until SQ status is 'green'.
A4: Audit trail: every delegated approval shows approver, timestamp, linked PR/contract, and change-set id in the playbook and is exportable as CSV for audit requests.

A5: UX: Sales team can initiate a Pricing Special Request (PSR) form from the Console that pre-fills customer tier, renewal term, and recommended discount band; submit returns expected SLA times (e.g., 24h for delegated, 72h for escalated).
A6: Finance integration: confirmed mapping to billing product SKUs and Stripe/Chargebee metadata so invoicing matches approved pricebook entries in 2 pilot accounts.
tasks: T1: Finalize Discount Authorization Matrix draft and circulate to Sales, Finance, Legal — owner: Marco Ruiz (PM). Due 2026-02-27.
T2: Implement PSR form in Console (front-end + backend endpoint) with field validation and SQ flagging — owner: ENG-frontend (subtask ENG-51340) — estimate 5 points.
T3: Build Pricebook Live-Sync webhook and nightly reconciliation job (staging) with idempotency checks — owner: ENG-billing (subtask ENG-51341) — estimate 8 points.
T4: Add audit CSV export and attach approval metadata to contract PRs in GitHub — owner: RevenueOps (implementer: Liang Chen).
T5: Run 3 pilot deals with Sales reps in EMEA and NA, collect feedback, and measure time-to-contract and finance reconciliation errors — owner: Sales Ops.
T6: Draft runbook for exception handling (how to revert incorrect pricebook entries; contact points) — owner: Marco Ruiz; deliverable in Confluence.

decision_log: D1 (2026-02-21): Use delegated approval bands instead of case-by-case approvals to reduce SLA friction. Rationale: most deals fall into repeatable bands; exception path remains.

D2 (2026-03-04): Implement pricebook live-sync with nightly reconciliation rather than immediate bi-directional sync. Rationale: prevents race conditions during contract sign and ensures Finance has a controlled reconciliation window.
D3 (2026-03-08): SQ gating threshold set at >25% discounts and any request involving data residency/compliance controls. Rationale: higher-concession deals carry legal/compliance risk.
